newsitem.title: JAPAN: US, Japan eye deregulation talk format by June.
newsitem.headline: US, Japan eye deregulation talk format by June.

text.p: U.S. and Japanese officials agreed on Wednesday to spell out a new format for their talks on deregulation in time for the Denver G7 (Group of Seven) leaders summit in June, a U.S. official said.
"We're looking to have the new mechanism in place by the G7 summit in Denver in June," the official told reporters after one day of talks with officials from some 13 Japanese ministries.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and President Bill Clinton agreed in Washington last month on the need to intensify the bilateral dialogue on deregulation, which has been going on under the 1993 U.S.-Japan Framework Agreement.
The official said Washington believes that "concrete" and "meaningful" deregulation would have a very positive effect on the Japanese economy as well as benefitting Japanese consumers.

He said the Japanese government's efforts to cut official red tape as one way to remove barriers to market access had "achieved some results." But he added, "However, we believe much more can and should be done to deregulate the Japanese economy."

The United States proposed on Wednesday that the talks be upgraded to include periodic meetings by senior officials and that initial discussions should focus on housing, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, telecommunications and financial services.
The United States also proposed setting up expert groups to discuss structural issues such as competition policy and distribution, and transparency in government practices.
"Our concern to date is that the government decides regulations in a black box and only those participants that the government wants to consult are invited in," another U.S. official said.
The two sides agreed on Wednesday to meet again in early June, probably in Tokyo, to further discuss the new format for the talks, the first official said.
